messages.content: The rehearsal is confirmed for Sunday, so our dates are Monday, March 10 through Thursday, March 13. We’re down to Drury Plaza and El Rey Court. Can you compare the real three-night cost and how practical each one is for the shorter trip?

For one room for two adults and your 14-year-old, the current three-night totals are $1,131 at Drury Plaza and $950 at El Rey Court. Those figures include taxes and the known mandatory charges; Drury’s total also includes three nights of parking at $28 per night, while parking at El Rey is included. El Rey saves $181 overall.
Is Drury’s location worth $181 when we only have Tuesday and Wednesday as full days?

It can be. Drury is near the Plaza, so you could park once and walk to the Plaza, Palace of the Governors, Cathedral Basilica, restaurants, and nearby galleries. That makes Monday evening and Thursday morning useful without another drive. El Rey is several miles southwest of the Plaza; expect roughly 10–15 minutes each way in ordinary traffic, plus time finding and paying for downtown parking.
We’ll probably arrive around 5:30 Monday and leave after breakfast Thursday. Tuesday would be museums and the Plaza. Wednesday might be Meow Wolf and then dinner downtown.

With that plan, Drury has the stronger practical advantage. Monday dinner, all of Tuesday’s central sightseeing, Wednesday dinner, and possibly Thursday breakfast can be done on foot. You would still drive to Meow Wolf Wednesday. From El Rey, Meow Wolf is convenient, but you would likely make downtown round trips Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday.
Put some numbers around that. I don’t want to pay $181 just to avoid a few short drives.

A reasonable El Rey estimate is three downtown round trips totaling about 60–90 minutes of driving, depending on traffic and where you eat. Add perhaps $30–$60 for downtown parking across the stay. That reduces the effective lodging savings from $181 to about $121–$151. Drury still costs more, but it buys back time during a trip with only two full days.
Breakfast matters too. Are we accounting for meals correctly?

Drury includes breakfast for all three guests and an evening food-and-drink reception. El Rey’s quoted rate does not include breakfast. If your family would otherwise spend even $35–$50 per morning, two breakfasts would absorb another $70–$100 of El Rey’s advantage. I would not assign full dinner value to Drury’s reception unless you know you would use it as a meal.
That makes Drury sound close enough. Before I choose it, verify that the two-queen room really allows two adults and a 14-year-old, and tell me the cancellation terms.

The displayed Drury two-queen room configuration accepts three guests when entered as two adults and one child age 14; no extra-person charge appears in the current total. The refundable rate shows cancellation without penalty until 11:59 p.m. local hotel time on March 8. After that deadline, the stated penalty is one night’s room rate plus tax. The booking page shows no resort or destination fee, and parking is $28 per night.
Any concern that the child age changes at checkout or that parking gets added twice?

The occupancy line should explicitly remain “2 adults, 1 child, age 14” on the final payment screen. Also check that the $1,131 total either itemizes the $84 parking estimate or clearly states parking is payable at the property; do not add it again if it is already included in your comparison total. Hotel parking charges are often collected separately even when shown in an estimated trip total.
All right. Which one would you book for this exact schedule, and what are the final checks?

I would book the refundable two-queen room at Drury Plaza for March 10–13. After breakfast value and likely downtown parking at El Rey, the remaining price gap is modest enough that Drury’s walkability is more useful on this compressed itinerary. Before submitting payment, confirm the dates, three-night stay, two-queen room, occupancy of two adults plus one 14-year-old, $1,131 comparison total, $28 nightly parking treatment, no mandatory fee, and the March 8 at 11:59 p.m. local cancellation deadline with a one-night-plus-tax late penalty. Save the final confirmation showing the actual amount charged now and anything due at the hotel.
